patients.summary: Wildlife biologist with well-controlled generalized tonic-clonic seizures on levetiracetam and hypertension on lisinopril who joined in mid-2024. Survived pneumonic plague contracted on a New Mexico field assignment in December 2024, then ARDS after a cold-water submersion a year later; the practice has not seen him since April 2025.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller would like to establish with the practice. Moved his care from his old doctor's office, which is too far a drive now. Two daily meds, seizure med and a BP pill, both filled through mail order. Insurance BCBS, verified. Booked new pt visit 6/11 at 9:00. Asked him to sign a records release for the prior office; form emailed.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
38 y/o M here to set up primary care. Wildlife biologist, a lot of field time, sometimes weeks away on assignments.

Seizures: generalized tonic-clonic seizure disorder, on Keppra (levetiracetam) 1000 mg BID for years. Well controlled, no events he can recall in a long time; father also has epilepsy. Takes it reliably, uses a pill box. No mood change on it that he notices. Drives.

HTN: lisinopril 10 mg daily, no cough, no dizziness. Doesn't check at home.

PSH: tonsils out at 12, open appendectomy at 25.
FHx: father epilepsy + HTN; mother T2DM; paternal grandfather MI at 62.
SHx: married. Never a smoker. Two or three drinks a week, beer mostly. No drugs.
Allergies: NKDA.

ROS negative except as above.

Exam: well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, tonsils absent. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear both sides. Abd soft, healed RLQ incision, nontender. Ext warm, no swelling. Neuro: alert, fluent, CN grossly intact, strength and gait normal.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Seizure disorder, generalized TC, controlled. Continue levetiracetam 1000 BID. Will take over refills.
2. HTN on lisinopril 10. Reading borderline high today after a rushed drive in; prior office readings were at goal. No change, recheck at follow-up. CMP.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, lipids, A1c given mom's diabetes. One-time HIV and hep C screen, he agrees. Flu/COVID this fall. Records requested from prior PCP.
RTC 3 months for BP.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Theo, your blood work from Tuesday looks good. Kidney function and potassium are normal on the lisinopril, blood counts are normal, cholesterol is fine, and your A1c shows no sign of diabetes. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. See you in September.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, thanks for the quick turnaround.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body: Records from former primary care office, 2019 through early 2024 (14 pages). Office notes for hypertension on lisinopril 10 mg daily and generalized seizure disorder on levetiracetam 1000 mg twice daily, no breakthrough events documented. BP readings in the 120s-130s/70s-80s. Yearly basic chemistry normal. Tdap given 2020. Allergies: none known. Filed; reviewed by PCP, nothing outstanding.

documents.title: Mail-order renewal
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mail-order pharmacy requesting new 90-day prescriptions: levetiracetam 1000 mg BID and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Seen 6/11, labs normal. Sent 90 days with 3 refills each per protocol.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: We missed you yesterday for your 3:30 appointment. Please reply or call to reschedule.

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sorry, I was out at a field site with no service and lost track of the date. Could I just come in for the flu shot and a BP check in October instead?

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That works. Nurse visit in early October for vaccines and a pressure check.

documents.title: Nurse visit: vaccines and BP
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for seasonal vaccines and a BP check in place of the missed September follow-up (June reading was borderline). Taking lisinopril every morning, no symptoms. Seated BP after 5 min within goal, reviewed with PCP who is fine to see him in the spring. Flu vaccine L deltoid, COVID R deltoid, lot numbers recorded. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Heading to the Southwest for a work project in December, aware to keep meds with him.

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Bilateral alveolar infiltrates with necrotizing features. Heart size not enlarged. No pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral alveolar infiltrates with necrotizing features.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note (out of state)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD — date of service 12/21/2024

Arrival by EMS. 38-year-old man, history of generalized seizure disorder on levetiracetam and hypertension on lisinopril. Fever, rigors and shortness of breath came on abruptly. Dry cough started yesterday and is now productive of blood-streaked sputum. Wife at bedside: he got sick fast overnight and has been more and more confused. He is in New Mexico on a work assignment and helped with a prairie dog eradication effort last week. No travel outside the country.

Meds: levetiracetam 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily. NKDA.
PSH: tonsillectomy, appendectomy. Never smoker, social alcohol.

Vitals on arrival: T 39.6 C, HR 124, BP 92/58, RR 30.
Exam: obtunded. Frothy pink sputum with coughing. Diffuse crackles in both lung fields.

Sputum gram stain and culture: pleomorphic gram-negative rod.
CXR: bilateral alveolar infiltrates, necrotizing appearance.

Impression: pneumonic plague suspected given rodent exposure; hypoxic respiratory failure; presumed septic shock.
Disposition: intubated in the ED, admitted to ICU. Infection control and public health notified.

[Received by fax 1/10/2025 at patient's request. Scanned.]

documents.title: Theo is in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is Theo's wife writing from his account. He got very sick in New Mexico over the weekend and is in the ICU on a ventilator. They think it is plague from the prairie dog work. They are giving him IV antibiotics. I wanted his doctor to know. They are still giving his seizure medicine through the tube.

documents.title: RE: Theo is in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know, and I am so sorry. Please ask the team there to send us records when they can, and call us once he is home so we can see him soon after. Thinking of you both.
